run report / narration, not term definitions

terms.desc: Agents communicate/coordinate via a protocol or message handoff.
The middle of WCAG's three conformance levels — A is lowest, AA next, AAA highest. AA is the level most public-sector accessibility rules point at, which is why it is the one usually quoted.
terms.source: W3C, "Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2", Conformance

terms.desc: Accuracy is a metric for evaluating classification models.
An algorithm to find the optimal transformations between the response variable and predictor variables in regression analysis.

Predictive model accuracy is consistently improved through targeted human feedback. This concept arises from the idea that active learning strategies often rely on expert annotators to provide feedback, which can introduce a bias towards more difficult or sensitive topics. As a result, models may perform less well on easier classes, neglecting important but less contentious tasks.
Using AdaBoost to improve performance in decision trees.
A statistical classification meta-algorithm that can be used in conjunction with many other types of learning algorithms to improve performance.
Optimizer combining Adam with decoupled weight decay; standard choice for transformer training.
Using AdaBoost to improve performance in regression.
Methods that aim to detect drum events in polyphonic music
A type of artificial neural network used to learn efficient codings of unlabeled data (unsupervised learning)

An autonomous AI system that perceives its environment, decides on actions, uses tools, and iterates toward a goal without step-by-step human guidance. Agents combine an LLM (for reasoning) with tools (search, code execution, APIs) and memory. The core loop: Observe → Plan → Act → Observe.
Replit Agent generation with extended builds and app testing modes.
OpenAI SDK for building agents with tools, handoffs, and tracing.
The hypothetical ability of an intelligent agent to understand or learn any intellectual task that a human being can
The simulation of human intelligence in machines that are programmed to think like humans and mimic their actions.
Managed AI providers/inference billed to Replit account (no personal key needed).

terms.expansion: Adaptive Inertia Weight Particle Swarm Optimization
terms.desc: An optimization algorithm using an individual search ability (ISA) to indicate whether each particle lacks global exploration or local exploitation abilities in each dimension.
Microsoft's managed Kubernetes platform; integrates with Azure storage, networking, and identity services.
Positional encoding adding biases to attention scores; enables better length extrapolation than RoPE.

The research field and practice of ensuring AI systems pursue intended goals and values rather than unintended ones. Techniques include RLHF, CAI, DPO, and interpretability research. Central challenge of safe AI development.
A method to visualize neural networks and aims to maximize the activation of certain neurons.
Computational algorithms that convert acoustic music signals into some form of music notation
A collection of connected computational units or nodes called neurons arranged in multiple computational layers.
Application Programming Interface
Explicit human approval steps before risky actions (merge, deploy, delete).
Hybrid processor combining CPU and GPU cores on a single die; AMD's term for integrated graphics processors.

An interactive experience of a real-world environment where the objects that reside in the real world are enhanced by computer-generated perceptual information sometimes across multiple sensory modalities.
Multiple-choice science question benchmark from AI2 with easy and challenge sets.
Score from human preference voting in LLM arenas; reflects real-world preference rather than benchmark tasks.

A set of HTML attributes that tell assistive technology what a component *is* and what state it is in, for interfaces built out of generic elements. WAI-ARIA 1.2 became a W3C Recommendation on 6 June 2023.
terms.source: W3C, "Accessible Rich Internet Applications (WAI-ARIA) 1.2", W3C Recommendation 6 June 2023
terms.misread: That adding ARIA makes a component behave correctly. It changes semantics only — nothing in the DOM changes, just the accessibility tree. Keyboard handling and focus management remain entirely yours to write.

terms.desc: A type of RNN designed to predict future inputs or states in sequential data.
Custom silicon designed for a specific task; examples include Bitcoin miners and neural accelerators.
Technology that converts spoken audio to text. Modern ASR uses transformer encoders (Whisper, Conformer). Key metrics: WER, RTF. Used in voice agents, meeting transcription, and accessibility tools.
Abstract Syntax Tree

A neural network operation that lets each token in a sequence compute a weighted sum of all other tokens, determining what to 'focus on.' Self-attention (within the same sequence) is the core of the Transformer. Multi-head attention runs several attention heads in parallel to capture different types of relationships.
Probability of confidence in a model to accurately predict positive outcomes for actual positive instances
Quantization method protecting important weights based on activation statistics.
Cloud computing platform offering compute, storage, and networking services; market leader with P4d/P5e GPU instances.
Microsoft's cloud platform with GPUs, specialized hardware, and tight integration with Windows/Office ecosystem.
An ensemble learning method combining multiple decision trees, typically using boosting algorithms like AdaBoost or Gradient Boosting.

A standardized test set and metric used to measure AI model capabilities. Common LLM benchmarks: MMLU (knowledge), HumanEval (code), GSM8K (math), MT-Bench (instruction following), Arena (human preference). Each probes a different capability axis.

A language representation model that pre-trains on unlabelled text while conditioning on both left and right context in every layer. That two-sided view is what set it apart from the left-to-right models before it.
terms.source: Devlin et al., "BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding", arXiv:1810.04805 (October 2018)

terms.desc: 16-bit format (8 exponent, 7 mantissa) designed for deep learning; better numerical stability than FP16.
An efficient multi-scale feature fusion method used in object detection, allowing bidirectional (top-down and bottom-up) information flow.
Task suite covering language, reasoning, and knowledge to evaluate emergent model capabilities.
A bidirectional recurrent neural network architecture utilizing LSTM units (see LSTM).
A score of the effectiveness of translating one language into another one.

A relevance ranking function for full-text search, used as the default ranking in SQLite's FTS5. In that implementation a numerically lower score means a better match, so results sort best-first in ascending order.
terms.source: SQLite documentation, "SQLite FTS5 Extension" — Sorting by Auxiliary Function Results

terms.desc: A probabilistic graphical model that represents a set of variables and their conditional dependencies via a directed acyclic graph (DAG).

A type of artificial neural network built by introducing random variations into the network either by giving the network's artificial neurons stochastic transfer functions or by giving them stochastic weights
A widely used algorithm for training feedforward neural networks by propagating errors backward through the network.

A way of splitting text into subword pieces by repeatedly merging the most frequent adjacent pair, borrowed from a compression algorithm. It makes vocabulary open-ended: a word never seen in training is represented as a sequence of smaller known pieces instead of being lost.
terms.source: Sennrich, Haddow & Birch, "Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units", arXiv:1508.07909 (August 2015; ACL 2016)

terms.desc: A probabilistic approach to matrix factorization, often used in recommender systems, incorporating Bayesian inference.
A gradient-based technique for training certain types of recurrent neural networks (e.g., LSTMs) by unrolling the network through time steps.
Google Cloud service enabling creation and execution of ML models in BigQuery using standard SQL queries.
An RNN variant that processes sequence data in both forward and backward directions, capturing context from past and future elements.
A regression technique that incorporates Bayesian methods with Ridge Regression (L2 regularization).
An autoencoder variant that adds a penalty term to the loss function to encourage robustness of the learned representation to small input variations.

Anthropic's alignment technique: the model critiques and revises its own outputs using a written 'constitution' of principles, reducing reliance on human labelers for harmful-content filtering. Pairs with RLHF.
A type of reinforcement learning agent operating in environments with continuous (non-discrete) action spaces.
An algorithm used to build decision trees for both classification and regression tasks by recursively partitioning the data space.
Explainability method that provides an interpretation of a neural net's internal state in terms of human-friendly concepts.
A technique potentially used in fairness research to test model robustness against specific biases by inserting counterfactual examples.
A neural network model architecture (part of Word2Vec) used for learning word embeddings by predicting a target word from its surrounding context words.
Automated release pipeline to ship changes.
A type of deep artificial neural network composed of multiple layers of convolutional restricted Boltzmann machines stacked together.
Distributed network of servers caching content globally to reduce latency for end users.
A common loss function used in classification tasks, measuring the difference between predicted probability distributions and the true distribution.
A key component within LSTM units that allows error signals to propagate back through time without vanishing or exploding gradient issues.
Technique used in recommendation systems predicting user preferences based on patterns from similar users or items.
Automated build/test checks on changes.
Text-based interface (e.g., terminal).
Neural networks whose output or internal processing is dependent on an auxiliary conditional input.
A type of neural network inspired by the mammalian cerebellum, often used for function approximation and control tasks, using associative memory principles.
A graphical model for sequence labeling that combines features of hidden Markov models (HMMs) and maximum entropy (MaxEnt) models. Also known as maximum-entropy Markov model (MEMM).
A class of artificial neural network (ANN), typically using convolutional layers, most commonly applied to analyze visual imagery.
Cloud-based software engineering agent (ChatGPT/CLI/IDE).

The maximum number of tokens a model can process in a single forward pass, including both the input prompt and generated output. Modern models range from 8K (GPT-3.5) to 1M+ tokens (Gemini 1.5 Pro). Determines how much 'memory' a model has per call.
Request batching technique that starts processing as soon as requests arrive rather than waiting for full batch.
A class of artificial neural network (ANN), typically using convolutional layers, most commonly applied to analyze visual imagery. (Synonym for CNN)

The protocol by which a server tells a browser that a page from another origin is allowed to read its response. If a resource does not speak CORS, the browser returns a network error instead of the data. GET, HEAD and POST are "safelisted" methods; anything else triggers a preflight check first.
terms.source: WHATWG Fetch Standard, §3.2 CORS protocol
terms.misread: That CORS is a restriction someone imposed on you. It is the mechanism for granting cross-origin access — the restriction is the browser's same-origin policy, which CORS exists to relax.

terms.desc: Learning rate schedule following cosine curve from initial to final value; common in modern training.
Stepwise reasoning style (often internal/hidden in products).

A loss function designed to minimize regret by comparing observed outcomes to their counterfactual alternatives. In essence, this concept measures the difference between actual and hypothetical outcomes under different scenarios. By using this approach in training models, we can identify which actions led to suboptimal results and make informed decisions for future iterations.
Central Processing Unit
An extension of the Restricted Boltzmann Machine where the visible and/or hidden units are conditioned on additional input variables.
A class of statistical modeling methods often used for structured prediction tasks like sequence labeling (e.g., in NLP), modeling conditional probabilities.
A hybrid neural network architecture combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), typically for spatio-temporal data.
Create, Read, Update, Delete
Sign language recognition and understanding (continuous using not only single words but whole phrases) getting knowledge about the meaning of signs essential for SLT.
An attack that makes a logged-in user's browser fire off a request they never intended, using the session they already have. The attacker never sees the response — they just cause the action.
terms.source: OWASP, "Cross Site Request Forgery (CSRF)"
terms.misread: That CSRF and XSS are the same family of bug. XSS injects and runs a script in the victim's browser; CSRF runs no script of its own, it just abuses an existing login. XSS can be used to defeat CSRF defences, which is why they get conflated.

terms.desc: Cascading Style Sheets
Comma-Separated Values
A loss function used for training sequence models (like RNNs) on tasks where the alignment between input and output sequences is variable or unknown (e.g., speech).
A recommendation model that integrates collaborative filtering with topic modeling (like LDA) to leverage item content information.
Maximum tokens the model can consider at once.

NVIDIA's parallel computing platform and programming model for running general-purpose work on the GPU. It is a platform and a model, not a language — it works through extensions to existing languages and its own compiler.
terms.source: NVIDIA, "CUDA C++ Programming Guide", Introduction
terms.misread: That CUDA stands for "Compute Unified Device Architecture". NVIDIA's current programming guide defines CUDA without expanding it at all; the expansion is legacy and no longer used by the vendor.

terms.desc: NVIDIA's GPU-optimized library for neural network operations; critical performance layer under frameworks.
Resampling method for training, validation and testing a model across different iterations on portions of the full data set.
Legacy/older style chat endpoint (still used in some stacks).
A technique possibly involving using auxiliary features alongside data augmentation to improve model training.
An autoencoder trained to reconstruct clean input from corrupted versions (Denoising AE), often with multiple hidden layers (Deep AE).
Standard interface for debuggers.
Replicating model across GPUs and processing different data batches; standard approach for scaling training.
Database
An undirected probabilistic graphical model (like RBM) with multiple layers of hidden variables, allowing for more complex representations.
A generative graphical model composed of multiple layers of latent variables ("beliefs"), typically trained greedily layer-by-layer using RBMs.

terms.expansion: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise
terms.desc: A density-based clustering algorithm that groups together points closely packed together, marking outliers as noise.
A type of GAN that uses convolutional and convolutional-transpose layers in its discriminator and generator, respectively, primarily for image generation.
Combines CNNs with Mixture Density Networks to model complex conditional probability distributions, often for image generation or regression tasks with uncertainty.
PyTorch's native distributed training wrapper for data parallelism across multiple GPUs/nodes.
A metaheuristic optimization algorithm belonging to the family of evolutionary algorithms, used for finding global optima, particularly in continuous spaces.
A neural network architecture often utilizing transposed convolutions (sometimes called deconvolutions) for tasks like image segmentation or visualization of CNN features.
An explainability method for deep learning models that attributes prediction differences to input feature differences based on a reference input.
Microsoft's library for efficient distributed training with ZeRO memory optimization and other techniques.
The HTTP method that asks the origin server to remove a resource.
terms.source: RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics" (IETF, June 2022), §9.3.5

terms.desc: A named design decision — at minimum a name and a value, such as color-text-primary: #000000 — stored in a tool-neutral JSON file so design tools and code can share one source of truth.
terms.source: Design Tokens Community Group, "Design Tokens Format Module", Draft Community Group Report 30 July 2026
terms.misread: That the DTCG format is a settled standard. It is a Draft Community Group Report, not a W3C Standard, and the draft itself says not to treat that version as authoritative.

terms.desc: Single piece of silicon containing the processor circuit; multiple dies packaged together form a chip.
A subfield of machine learning based on artificial neural networks with multiple layers (deep architectures) enabling learning of complex patterns.
An artificial neural network (ANN) with multiple hidden layers between the input and output layers.

The distributed directory that turns names into addresses, so that a name does not have to carry any routing information inside it. It has three parts: the tree-shaped namespace and its records, the name servers that hold the data, and the resolvers that go and fetch it. It replaced a single shared HOSTS.TXT file that stopped scaling in the 1980s.
terms.source: RFC 1034, "Domain Names — Concepts and Facilities" (IETF, November 1987)

terms.desc: The programming interface that represents a loaded page as a tree of nodes and objects, so code can read and change its structure, style and content.
terms.source: MDN Web Docs, "Introduction to the DOM" (Mozilla)
terms.misread: That the DOM is part of JavaScript. It is a separate, language-independent Web API. Node.js runs JavaScript with no DOM at all, and the DOM can be driven from other languages.

terms.desc: An alternative to RLHF that reparameterises the reward model so the optimal policy has a closed form, turning alignment into a simple classification loss. It needs no separate reward model and no sampling from the model during fine-tuning, which is why it is described as lighter and more stable than the RL pipeline it replaces.
terms.source: Rafailov et al., "Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model", arXiv:2305.18290 (May 2023)

terms.desc: Specialized processor for networking and data-plane operations; offloads packet processing from CPUs in data centers.
A reinforcement learning algorithm that uses a deep neural network to approximate the Q-value (action-value) function.
Represents the sensitivity or detection rate of a model (synonym for True Positive Rate or Recall).
Regularization technique randomly zeroing activations during training to prevent overfitting.
A deep learning architecture based on stacking blocks of simple modules (like MLPs) trained sequentially, layer by layer.
A supervised learning model using a tree-like structure of decisions and their possible consequences to classify or regress data.
An explainability technique that decomposes the prediction of a neural network based on Taylor series expansion, related to Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP).
A mathematical transform used for signal processing and feature extraction, decomposing signals into different frequency components at multiple scales.
AWS service for renting virtual machines; g4dn, p3, p4d instances used for ML workloads.
Processing data near the source (device or local server) rather than in centralized cloud.
Targeted edits to specific UI/components without rewriting everything.
AWS's managed Kubernetes offering; integrates with VPC and EC2 for networking and compute.

terms.expansion: Efficiently Learning an Encoder that Classifies Token Replacements Accurately
terms.desc: A transformer-based pre-training method that learns by distinguishing real input tokens from plausible fake tokens generated by another small network (discriminator task).
A feedforward neural network training algorithm where hidden node parameters are randomly assigned and only output weights are learned analytically, often very fast.
Contextual word embedding technique generating deep, character-based representations that vary based on the sentence context.
Comparative ranking from pairwise comparisons (A vs B); used in LLM arenas like ChatBot Arena.
An activation function similar to ReLU but with negative values, which can help push mean activations closer to zero, potentially speeding up learning.
An iterative method for finding maximum likelihood or MAP estimates of parameters in statistical models with latent (unobserved) variables.
Vector representation of text/images for similarity search.
Layer converting discrete tokens to dense vectors; foundational for transformer input representation.
A method for discretizing continuous features by finding split points that minimize the class information entropy within the resulting intervals.
End of Day
A transformer-based language model (often associated with Baidu) that incorporates external knowledge (e.g., knowledge graph facts) during pre-training.
Estimated Time of Arrival
A data integration process involving extracting data from sources, transforming it into a proper format, and loading it into a target system (like a data warehouse).
Empathic Voice Interface
An ensemble learning method similar to Random Forests, but introduces more randomness in selecting node splits (both attribute and split point).
The harmonic mean of precision and recall, used as a performance metric for classification tasks, especially with imbalanced datasets.
A type of reinforcement learning agent operating in environments with a finite number of discrete actions.
Frequently Asked Questions
Layers where all the inputs from one layer are connected to every activation unit of the next layer.
A neural network architecture consisting entirely of convolutional layers (and pooling/upsampling), without any fully-connected layers.
An LSTM network where connections between time steps or layers might involve fully connected transformations, combining sequential and dense processing.
A clustering algorithm allowing data points to belong to multiple clusters with varying degrees of membership (fuzziness).
A neural network that only performs convolution (and subsampling or upsampling) operations, often used for semantic segmentation. (Similar to FC-CNN)

Providing a small number of input-output examples in the prompt so the model learns the pattern in-context. Two examples = 2-shot; five examples = 5-shot. Dramatically improves accuracy on structured tasks (classification, extraction, formatting) without any weight updates.
Fully-connected layers in transformer blocks after attention; typically 4x hidden dimension.
An efficient algorithm to compute the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and its inverse, widely used in signal processing and feature engineering.

Code completion mode where the model fills a gap between a prefix and a suffix already written. Used in IDE autocomplete (Cursor, Copilot). Training uses a special prompt structure: <PRE> prefix <SUF> suffix <MID>.

Continuing to train a pre-trained model on a task-specific dataset to adapt its weights for a particular domain, style, or capability. Distinct from RAG (no retrieval) and from LoRA (which fine-tunes a small adapter). Common use cases: medical QA, code style, customer support tone.
Algorithm reducing attention memory and compute; enables longer context and faster inference.
A unit of measure of the amount of mathematical computations (like additions, multiplications) often used to describe the complexity of a neural network model.
A unit of measure of computer performance, indicating how many floating-point operations a processor can perform per second.
An artificial neural network where connections between nodes do not form a cycle; information moves only forward from input to output layers.
Proportion of actual positives predicted as negatives (1 - Recall/TPR).
Half-precision floating point; standard for mixed-precision training and inference.
Ultra-low precision format for inference; newer support in H100 and newer GPUs.
Reconfigurable hardware that can be reprogrammed post-manufacture; flexible alternative to ASICs.
A neural network component, common in object detection, that builds multi-scale feature representations with rich semantics at all levels via lateral connections.
Proportion of actual negatives predicted as positives.
Include examples to steer output.
PyTorch's advanced distributed training technique sharding model states; similar to ZeRO.
Finite State Machine
A finite automaton with two tapes (input and output), used for modeling sequence-to-sequence transformations (e.g., in NLP/speech).
File Transfer Protocol

SQLite's full-text search extension, implemented as a virtual table module. It indexes text columns and answers phrase, prefix, proximity (NEAR) and boolean queries via the MATCH operator, ranking results with BM25 by default.
terms.source: SQLite documentation, "SQLite FTS5 Extension"

terms.desc: Model returns structured arguments to call external functions.
Metric in segmentation/object detection tasks. Weighted average of IoU's over classes, where weights depend on class frequency.
For Your Information
A metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by natural selection, using concepts like mutation, crossover, and selection to evolve solutions.
An explainability technique that aims to derive global insights about a model's behavior by aggregating multiple local explanations (e.g., SHAP, LIME) from individual predictions.
An explainability method, often used with CNNs, to identify which input regions (e.g., pixels in an image) contribute most significantly to a specific output class.

terms.expansion: Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape
terms.desc: An extension of GAMs allowing not just the mean (location) but also other distribution parameters (like scale/variance and shape/skewness) to be modeled with additive predictors.

A deep-learning-based generative model using "indirect" training through the discriminator another neural network that is able to tell how much an input is "realistic" which itself is also being updated dynamically.

A pooling operation often used in CNNs before the final classification layer, reducing each feature map to a single value by averaging, which helps reduce overfitting and enforces correspondence between feature maps and categories.
A model likely combining gradient boosting techniques with randomly initialized convolutional features, possibly for time-series or image analysis.
Google's cloud infrastructure with TPUs, GPUs, and managed ML services; strong for TensorFlow workloads.
GCP's object storage service; similar role to S3 with integration to GCP ML services.
An optimization algorithm used to minimize some function by iteratively moving in the direction of steepest descent as defined by the negative of the gradient.
General Data Protection Regulation
Explainability method that aggregates local explanations (of single prediction) into a global explanation with the goal of finding biases and systematic errors in decision making.
Neural networks possibly designed to better learn or represent high-frequency components in data, potentially by manipulating gradients during training.
C++ tensor library for efficient inference on consumer hardware; foundation for Ollama.

A single-file binary format for model weights, built for fast loading in ggml-based inference engines such as llama.cpp. Unlike tensor-only formats it stores its metadata as typed key-value pairs alongside the tensors, which is what lets a file describe its own architecture. Created by Georgi Gerganov as the successor to the earlier GGML, GGMF and GGJT formats.
terms.source: ggml project, "GGUF" specification (docs/gguf.md); Hugging Face Hub documentation, "GGUF"
terms.misread: That GGUF is Ollama's format. Ollama consumes it; it comes from the ggml/llama.cpp project. The commonly quoted expansion "GGML Unified Format" appears nowhere in the format specification.

terms.desc: AI coding assistant in Replit (autocomplete/chat style).
Operational model where Git is the single source of truth; changes pull from Git rather than push.
GCP's managed Kubernetes service for containerized workloads; simplifies cluster management.
A statistical method for examining texture that considers the spatial relationship of pixels, used for feature extraction in image analysis.

terms.expansion: A task of transforming raw glosses into meaningful sentences.
terms.desc: In sign language processing, the task of converting a sequence of sign glosses (word-level representations) into a grammatically correct spoken language sentence.
An unsupervised learning algorithm for obtaining vector representations for words, trained on aggregated global word-word co-occurrence statistics from a corpus.
A probabilistic model that assumes all the data points are generated from a mixture of a finite number of Gaussian distributions with unknown parameters.
Benchmark designed to resist internet search; requires genuine expert knowledge rather than memorization.
A non-parametric, Bayesian approach to regression where the model learns a distribution over functions, providing uncertainty estimates along with predictions.
An autoregressive language model that uses deep learning to produce human-like text.
Post-training quantization method for INT4; preserves model quality better than naive quantization.
Specialized processor optimized for parallel computation; foundational for modern deep learning training and inference.
Attention variant where multiple query heads share key/value heads; reduces KV cache size and computation.

A visualization technique for CNNs that uses the gradients flowing into the final convolutional layer to produce a coarse localization map highlighting important regions in the input image for predicting the concept.
Training technique reducing memory by recomputing activations instead of storing them; trades compute for memory.
Query language for APIs allowing clients to request specific fields; alternative to REST.

Connecting a model's outputs to verifiable external sources (documents, databases, APIs) to reduce hallucination. RAG is the most common grounding approach. Grounded outputs include citations to source material.

A framework for remote procedure calls: client code calls a method on a server on another machine as though it were a local object. Services and their methods are declared up front, and by default the wire format is Protocol Buffers rather than JSON.
terms.source: gRPC documentation, "Introduction to gRPC"
terms.misread: That the g stands for Google. The official documentation does not expand it — the letter's meaning has changed with each release.

terms.desc: A variant of PPO introduced with DeepSeekMath that improves mathematical reasoning while cutting PPO's memory use.
terms.source: Shao et al., "DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models", arXiv:2402.03300 (February 2024), abstract

terms.desc: Benchmark of 8.5K grade school math word problems; simpler than MATH, useful baseline.
Explicit constraints: what the agent must not touch.
Graphical User Interface

When a language model generates plausible-sounding but factually incorrect or fabricated content. A fundamental failure mode of LLMs. Mitigated by RAG (grounding in retrieved facts) and structured output constraints.
An annotation system that describes sign language symbols.
A neural network architecture, typically used for document classification, employing attention mechanisms at both word and sentence levels to capture important information hierarchically.
Stacked memory architecture with dramatically higher bandwidth than GDDR; used in advanced GPUs.
Enhanced version of HBM2 with higher density and bandwidth; used in A100, H100 GPUs.
Latest HBM generation offering 4x bandwidth of HBM2e; featured in NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI325X.
A method of cluster analysis which seeks to build a hierarchy of clusters, either agglomerative (bottom-up) or divisive (top-down).
A non-parametric Bayesian approach for modeling grouped data, often used in topic modeling to allow for an infinite number of topics shared across groups.
Package manager for Kubernetes; simplifies deployment and configuration management via templates.
Likely refers to a specific dataset focused on Hip Hop music, used for tasks like music information retrieval (MIR), genre classification, or beat tracking.
Human approvals or review embedded in the workflow.
An extension of LDA that organizes topics into a hierarchy, allowing documents to be associated with paths of topics at different levels of granularity.
A way to prove a message came from someone holding a shared secret key and has not been altered, by combining that key with a hash function. It authenticates; it does not hide anything.
terms.source: NIST FIPS 198-1, "The Keyed-Hash Message Authentication Code (HMAC)" (February 2009); construction defined in RFC 2104
terms.misread: That HMAC encrypts. It produces a verification tag alongside the message — the message itself stays readable.

terms.desc: A statistical Markov model in which the system being modeled is assumed to be a Markov process with unobserved (hidden) states, commonly used for sequential data like speech or NLP.
A form of recurrent artificial neural network popularized by John Hopfield, serving as content-addressable ("associative") memory systems with binary threshold nodes.
Computing infrastructure for scientific and AI workloads requiring massive parallelism and throughput.
HyperText Markup Language

The request/response protocol the web runs on. A client asks for something, a server answers. HTTP is stateless: the protocol itself remembers nothing between requests, which is why sessions have to be rebuilt on every call using cookies or tokens.
terms.source: RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics" (IETF, June 2022), §1.1

terms.desc: HTTP over TLS encryption.
Heads-Up Display
Benchmark of 164 Python programming tasks for code generation models; standard for code capability eval.
A fundamental assumption in many statistical and machine learning models, stating that random variables in a sequence have the same probability distribution and are mutually independent.
Practice of defining cloud infrastructure in version-controlled code; enables reproducibility and CI/CD.
Cloud service controlling who accesses what resources via authentication and fine-grained authorization.
Model adapts behavior based on examples inside the prompt.
Identifier
An early algorithm used to generate a decision tree from a dataset, using information gain to select the best attribute at each step.
Editor + tools for coding (debugger, lint, etc.).

A property of a request method: doing it many times has the same intended effect on the server as doing it once. It is what makes a client safe to retry after a timeout, because a duplicate cannot do extra damage.
terms.source: RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics" (IETF, June 2022), §9.2.2
terms.misread: That idempotent means "returns the same answer every time". It is about the effect on the server, not the response you get back.

terms.desc: A metric possibly measuring how much a model's output or internal state depends on its input features, potentially used in explainability or sensitivity analysis.
A metric likely measuring the degree to which a model's output is independent of its input features, possibly related to robustness or fairness evaluation.
A metric used in XAI to measure how poorly an explanation (e.g., feature attributions) reflects the actual behavior of the model when inputs are perturbed.

The process of running a trained model to generate predictions or outputs — as opposed to training, which updates model weights. In LLM contexts, inference is the forward pass that produces tokens given a prompt. Key metrics: latency (TTFT), throughput (TPS), and cost per token.
High-performance, low-latency networking standard for HPC and data center; supports RDMA for GPU clusters.
Extreme quantization reducing weights to 4 bits; enables fitting larger models but with quality trade-offs.
Reducing weights and activations to 8-bit integers; common middle ground for quantization.
Internet of Things
Metric in segmentation/object detection tasks. Ratio of areas of intersection and union of two (segmentation) boxes, corresponding to e.g. prediction and label.
Internet Protocol
Rate limit for image generation/processing.
Graphcore's processor architecture designed for AI training with support for mixed-precision computation.
An academia-industry partnership focused on creating digital skin imaging standards and datasets for melanoma research, often used in computer vision challenges.

A prompt or technique that circumvents an LLM's safety guardrails to produce content the model would normally refuse. Examples: role-play framing, token injection, nested instructions. Studying jailbreaks helps build more robust models.
Common structured data format.
Specification for validating JSON structure and types; widely used for API documentation and validation.
Formal schema for validating JSON structure.
A compact, URL-safe way to carry a set of claims — statements about a subject — as a JSON object between two parties. The claims are encoded so they can be signed, MACed, or encrypted.
terms.source: RFC 7519, "JSON Web Token (JWT)" (IETF, May 2015), Terminology
terms.misread: That a JWT is encrypted and therefore private. The common signed form (JWS) is only signed: anyone holding the token can read every claim inside it. Encryption is a separate, less-used form (JWE).

terms.desc: A non-parametric, instance-based learning algorithm where classification or regression is based on the majority vote or average of the 'k' nearest neighbors in the feature space.
Open-source container orchestration platform for deploying, scaling, and managing containerized applications.

Ref. https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19756v1 - A novel neural network architecture inspired by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem, potentially offering better interpretability and scaling properties compared to MLPs by using learnable activation functions on edges instead of fixed ones on nodes.
A non-parametric way to estimate the probability density function of a random variable by placing kernels (usually Gaussian) over each data point.
Knowledge Graph
A measure of how one probability distribution diverges from a second, expected probability distribution; often used as a loss or regularization term (e.g., in VAEs).
A non-parametric supervised learning method used for classification and regression. (Synonym for k-NN)

Training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the output distribution of a larger 'teacher' model. The student learns from soft probability distributions (not just hard labels), transferring the teacher's generalization. Used to compress frontier models into deployable sizes — e.g., DeepSeek-R1's distilled variants.
Key Performance Indicator
A combination of Ridge Regression (L2-regularized linear regression) with the kernel trick, allowing it to learn non-linear functions in high-dimensional spaces.
Training approach balancing winning and avoiding losing; addresses distribution shifts in preference data.

The per-request memory a serving system keeps so it does not recompute attention over the whole conversation on every new token. It is large and it grows and shrinks unpredictably, so mismanaging it — through fragmentation and duplication — is what limits how many requests a GPU can serve at once.
terms.source: Kwon et al., "Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention", arXiv:2309.06180 (September 2023)

terms.desc: Normalization technique normalizing across features for each sample; standard in transformers.
A dimensionality reduction technique also used for classification, which aims to find a linear combination of features that characterizes or separates two or more classes.
Likely a hybrid approach combining LDA for topic modeling with Differential Evolution, possibly for optimizing LDA parameters or using topics within the DE process.
Strategy for adjusting learning rate during training (warmup, linear decay, cosine annealing, etc.).
Gradient boosting framework that uses tree based learning algorithms, originally developed by Microsoft. Known for efficiency and speed.
An XAI technique that explains individual predictions of any black-box classifier by learning a simpler, interpretable model locally around the prediction.
Process of etching circuit patterns onto silicon; measured in nanometers (5nm, 3nm, etc.); smaller = more density.
Continuously updated code generation benchmark with recently released programming problems.
A deep learning model trained on vast amounts of text data, capable of understanding and generating human-like text for various NLP tasks.
Specialized MLOps for LLMs; addresses prompt versioning, token budgets, latency SLAs, and cost optimization.
Large Language Models

A fine-tuning method that freezes the pre-trained weights and injects small trainable rank-decomposition matrices into each Transformer layer. On GPT-3 175B the paper reports 10,000× fewer trainable parameters and 3× less GPU memory than full fine-tuning.
terms.source: Hu et al., "LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models", arXiv:2106.09685 (June 2021)

terms.desc: Agentic app builder that generates full-stack apps from prompts.
Groq's proprietary tensor streaming architecture designed specifically for LLM inference with extreme throughput.
An XAI technique for deep neural networks that decomposes the output prediction backward through the layers to assign relevance scores to input features.
A technique in NLP using singular value decomposition (SVD) to analyze relationships between documents and terms, identifying latent semantic structures.

An indexing and retrieval method using LSA (SVD) to identify patterns in term-document relationships, improving information retrieval by handling synonymy and polysemy. (Often used interchangeably with LSA).

A protocol that lets one language server provide completion, diagnostics and navigation to any editor that speaks it, over JSON-RPC. It exists to kill the M×N problem: before it, every language had to be reimplemented separately for every editor.
terms.source: Microsoft, "Language Server Protocol" — Overview

terms.desc: A recurrent neural network can process not only single data points (such as images) but also entire sequences of data (such as speech or video).
Application of machine learning to construct ranking models for information retrieval systems, ordering items based on relevance.

A prototype-based supervised classification algorithm, related to Self-Organizing Maps (SOM), that uses competitive learning to move prototypes towards or away from training instances based on class labels.
An autoregressive model based on autoencoders, using carefully constructed masks to ensure that reconstructions respect autoregressive constraints, allowing for tractable density estimation.
Average of the absolute error between the actual and predicted values.
A type of normalizing flow model for density estimation that uses masked autoregressive transformations (like MADE) to ensure invertibility and efficient computation.
State space model architecture with selective state updates; offers linear complexity as transformer alternative.
A method for estimating unknown parameters in Bayesian statistics, finding the mode (peak) of the posterior distribution, incorporating prior knowledge.
Percentage of the error between the actual and predicted values (often expressed as a percentage).
Non-parametric regression technique, extends linear models. Note that the name is trademarked, open source implementations are often called "EARTH".
Another name for Gradient Boosted Decision Trees (GBDT), particularly associated with Friedman's original work, emphasizing the additive nature of the tree ensemble.
Benchmark of 12.5K mathematical problems at high school competition level; evaluates reasoning.
Entropy a scientific concept as well as a measurable physical property that is most commonly associated with a state of disorderrandomnessor uncertainty.
Conditional neural networks where masking techniques might be applied, possibly to control information flow or enforce specific dependencies based on the condition.
A class of algorithms for sampling from a probability distribution by constructing a Markov chain that has the desired distribution

An open standard for connecting AI applications to outside systems — data sources, tools and prompt workflows — so an integration is written once and works across every client that speaks it. Its own documentation likens it to USB-C for AI applications.
terms.source: Model Context Protocol documentation, "What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?"

terms.desc: Mechanistic interpretability is the study of how a neural network’s internal components produce its behavior. Researchers analyze features, circuits, attention patterns, and activations to identify how information is represented and transformed. The goal is to explain model behavior at a deeper level than observing inputs and outputs alone.
NVIDIA's framework for large model training with tensor/pipeline parallelism and mixed precision.
Multi-Factor Authentication
Standard transformer attention mechanism with multiple parallel attention heads.

terms.expansion: Mutual Information based Transductive Feature Selection

terms.desc: Metric in segmentation/object detection tasks. Mean of IoU's over classes.

A short permissive open-source licence: anyone may use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense and sell the software, provided the copyright notice and licence text travel with it. The software is supplied as-is, with all warranties disclaimed.
terms.source: Open Source Initiative, "The MIT License"
terms.misread: That MIT is an acronym. It is named after the institution where it originated; the OSI licence text expands nothing.

terms.desc: Using both FP16/BF16 and FP32 during training for speed and memory savings with numerical stability.

An architecture that routes input tokens to specialized sub-networks (experts) based on their content, activating only a fraction of the model's total parameters per token. This approach enables massive model scaling while maintaining computational efficiency, as seen in models like Switch Transformers and Mixtral, where different experts specialize in different types of linguistic patterns or knowledge domains.
The study of computer algorithms that can improve automatically through experience and by the use of data.
Attention variant used in DeepSeek models compressing query, key, value with learnable projections.
Practices for managing ML model lifecycle: training, versioning, deployment, monitoring, retraining.
A fully connected class of feedforward artificial neural network
Benchmark with 57K multiple-choice questions across STEM, humanities, social sciences; standard LLM eval.
Routes tokens to subsets of expert networks for scale/efficiency.
Metric in segmentation/object detection tasks. Average ratio of correctly classified pixels by class.
Attention with single key/value head shared by all query heads; extreme version of GQA.
Average of the squares of the error between the actual and predicted values
Multi-turn conversation benchmark evaluating instruction following and coherence over extended dialogue.

AI systems that process and generate across multiple modalities: text, image, audio, and video. GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro, and Claude 3.5 Sonnet are multimodal — they accept image+text input and produce text. Video-capable models (Gemini 1.5 Pro, GPT-4o) add a third modality.
Minimum Viable Product
A technique for automating the design of artificial neural networks.
Maps private IPs to public IPs; common in routers/VMs.

terms.expansion: Na ÌˆÄ±ve Bayes with Kernel Estimation

terms.desc: GPU-optimized collective communication library for multi-GPU and multi-node workloads.
Natural Language Processing
An approach to translation with the use of a neural network to predict a sequence of words.
A technique used in Object Detection for removing redundand overlapping bounding boxes

terms.expansion: Neural Network based Multi-Onset Detection Function Fusion

terms.desc: Tool uses hosted integrations/browser execution instead of your personal API keys.
Lightweight accelerator for on-device AI inference; common in smartphones and edge devices.
Cross-entropy Metric based on the logistic function that measures the error between the actual and predicted values.
A method that uses of deep neural networks for transfering style.
High-bandwidth, low-latency interconnect between NVIDIA GPUs; enables efficient multi-GPU training.
Networking fabric for connecting up to 8 GPUs with NVLink; allows all-to-all GPU communication.
APIs for calling OpenAI models and tools.
Open Authorization

A framework that lets a third-party application get limited access to a service on your behalf without you handing over your password. Instead of credentials, the app receives an access token carrying a specific scope and lifetime.
terms.source: RFC 6749, "The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework" (IETF, October 2012)
terms.misread: That OAuth logs you in. It is an authorization framework — it delegates access to resources. The spec explicitly puts how the user is authenticated outside its own scope. Logging in on top of OAuth is a separate layer (OpenID Connect).

terms.desc: The Linux Foundation body that publishes the open standards for container formats and runtimes, founded in 2015 by Docker, CoreOS and others. It maintains three specifications: runtime, image and distribution.
terms.source: Open Container Initiative, "About / Overview"
terms.misread: In cloud writing OCI also abbreviates Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, an unrelated thing. Which one is meant has to come from context.

terms.desc: Optical Character Recognition

A CSS colour function that specifies an Oklab colour by lightness, chroma and hue. Oklab is a device-independent colour space, so equal numeric steps look like equal visual steps — unlike HSL, where changing only the hue visibly changes the brightness too.
terms.source: W3C, "CSS Color Module Level 4", Candidate Recommendation Draft 6 August 2026, §9

terms.desc: Pay-as-you-go cloud compute with no commitment; highest pricing but maximum flexibility.

A common language for describing machine-learning models as computation graphs, so a model trained in one framework can be deployed by a runtime built for another. It exists to spare teams a separate deployment path per framework.
terms.source: ONNX documentation, "ONNX Concepts"

terms.desc: Out of Memory
Specification for describing REST APIs in machine-readable format; enables tooling and documentation.
Object-Relational Mapping
RLHF alternative removing reward model; directly optimizes preference signal from model logits.
Operating System
Network where nodes connect directly without a central server.
Metric in segmentation/object detection tasks. Ratio of correctly classified over total number of pixels.
An attention algorithm that manages a model's key-value cache the way an operating system manages virtual memory — in pages. This stops the cache fragmenting and lets separate requests share pages.
terms.source: Kwon et al., "Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention", arXiv:2309.06180 (September 2023)

terms.desc: A set of techniques that adapt large pre-trained models to downstream tasks by updating only a small subset of parameters while keeping the majority frozen. PEFT methods like LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation) and adapters significantly reduce computational costs and storage requirements compared to full fine-tuning, making it feasible to customize massive models on limited hardware.
The process of computing the principal components and using them to perform a change of basis on the data sometimes using only the first few principal components and ignoring the rest.
Standard interconnect for attaching GPUs and other devices to CPUs; bottleneck for data transfer.
Portable Document Format
Family of techniques reducing trainable parameters during fine-tuning; includes LoRA, prefix tuning, adapters.

terms.expansion: Pre-training with Extracted Gap-Sentences for Abstractive Summarization

terms.desc: Language model evaluation metric measuring how well the model predicts text; lower is better.
Data that can identify an individual.
Splitting model layers across GPUs; enables processing multiple batches simultaneously for improved throughput.

An addition to OAuth 2.0 that stops an intercepted authorization code from being useful to whoever grabbed it. The client commits to a secret at the start and must prove it at the end. Pronounced "pixy". It was written for public clients such as mobile apps, where another app on the same device can intercept the redirect.
terms.source: RFC 7636, "Proof Key for Code Exchange by OAuth Public Clients" (IETF, September 2015)

terms.desc: Read-only analysis/planning mode for safer debugging and audits.
Portable Network Graphics
Proof of Concept
Technique adding position information to token embeddings; enables transformer to understand sequence order.

The standard operating-system interface — system calls, a shell, and the common command-line utilities — that lets source code be written once and compiled on any conforming system. The current edition is IEEE Std 1003.1-2024 (Open Group Base Specifications, Issue 8).
terms.source: The Open Group Base Specifications Issue 8, IEEE Std 1003.1-2024, Base Definitions §1 (Scope)
terms.misread: That POSIX compliance means compiled programs are portable. It is portability at the *source* level; binary portability is explicitly out of scope.

terms.desc: The HTTP method that asks a server to process the data you are sending, according to whatever that particular resource does with it. POST is deliberately open-ended — the spec does not say it means "create".
terms.source: RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics" (IETF, June 2022), §9.3.3
terms.misread: That POST always means "create a record". The spec only says the server processes the submitted data by its own rules; creating is one common case, not the definition.

terms.desc: The four principles WCAG is built on. Content must be presentable in a way users can perceive; the interface must be operable; content and operation must be understandable; and it must be robust enough to keep working across technologies and assistive tools.
terms.source: W3C, "Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2", WCAG 2 Layers of Guidance

terms.desc: RLHF algorithm optimizing model outputs against human preferences with stability constraints.
Git workflow for proposing changes for review.

The first and most expensive training phase — the model learns language, facts, and reasoning from trillions of tokens of raw text using next-token prediction (causal LM loss). Produces a foundation model. Followed by supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and alignment (RLHF/DPO) to produce a chat assistant.

KV cache reuse mechanism where a provider stores computed attention states for a repeated prompt prefix (e.g. a long system prompt) and reuses them across calls. Reduces TTFT and API cost by 50-90% for requests sharing a common prefix. Supported by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Gemini.

terms.expansion: Parametric Rectified Linear Unit-Yor Topic Modeling

terms.desc: The practice of designing and refining prompts to elicit better, more reliable outputs from LLMs. Techniques include: chain-of-thought ('think step by step'), few-shot examples, structured output instructions, persona framing, and negative examples. A mix of art and empirical science.

Google's language- and platform-neutral format for serialising structured data. You declare the shape once in a .proto file and it generates native code for each language. Smaller and faster on the wire than JSON, and designed so a schema can evolve without breaking data already written.
terms.source: Google, "Protocol Buffers Overview"

terms.desc: Removing weights or entire neurons/attention heads from a model after training to reduce size and inference cost. Unstructured pruning zeroes individual weights; structured pruning removes entire channels/layers (easier to accelerate on hardware). Often combined with quantization and distillation for full compression pipelines.
Push To Talk
Machine learning paradigma to learn from only positive and unlabeled data.
The HTTP method that asks a server to create or replace a resource's entire state with the data you sent. Unlike POST, it is idempotent: sending it twice leaves the same result as sending it once.
terms.source: RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics" (IETF, June 2022), §9.3.4

terms.desc: An industry term for a website built to install and behave like a native app, typically using a Web App Manifest and a service worker.
terms.source: W3C, "Web Application Manifest" (W3C Working Draft 13 August 2026) — the manifest is specified; the term PWA is not defined there
terms.misread: That PWA is a W3C standard you can conform to. It is not defined by any specification — the underlying pieces (manifest, service workers) are standardised, but "PWA" itself is community terminology with no formal conformance criteria.

terms.desc: Combining quantization and LoRA for extreme parameter efficiency; enables fine-tuning on single GPU.
Reducing model precision (FP32 to INT8 or FP8) to save memory and accelerate computation.

Combining a model's built-in (parametric) knowledge with an external, searchable store it retrieves from at answer time. The original work paired a pre-trained seq2seq model with a dense vector index of Wikipedia. The gains it claimed were as much about provenance and updatable knowledge as about accuracy.
terms.source: Lewis et al., "Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks", arXiv:2005.11401 (May 2020)

terms.desc: Random-Access Memory
Role-Based Access Control
Technology allowing direct memory-to-memory data transfer between machines without CPU involvement.
Pattern interleaving reasoning with tool actions.
An activation function that allow fast and effective training of deep neural architectures on large and complex datasets.
Read-Eval-Print Loop
Browser-based IDE + hosting with built-in AI features.
AI that scaffolds and builds apps from natural language inside Replit.

Representation engineering is the practice of identifying and modifying a model’s internal representations to influence its behavior. It may involve detecting activation patterns associated with concepts such as truthfulness, emotion, or refusal. Those patterns can then be strengthened, weakened, or redirected during inference without fully retraining the model.
Cloud VM commitment for 1-3 years offering significant discount vs on-demand pricing.
Skip connection allowing gradients to flow directly; enables training of very deep networks.
Unified OpenAI API endpoint for model interactions and tool use.
Web API style based on HTTP resources.

A technique that enhances large language models by retrieving relevant information from external knowledge bases before generating responses. This approach combines the parametric knowledge of LLMs with non-parametric external data sources to improve factual accuracy, reduce hallucinations, and enable up-to-date responses without requiring frequent model retraining.
Request For Comments

The timestamp format used across internet protocols — 2026-08-16T14:30:00Z — defined as a deliberately narrow profile of ISO 8601. Every time carries a stated offset from UTC, and the Z suffix means an offset of exactly 00:00. It exists because full ISO 8601 is too permissive to interoperate on.
terms.source: RFC 3339, "Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps" (IETF, July 2002)

terms.desc: An additive color model used for display of images

terms.expansion: Repeated Incremental Pruning to Produce Error Reduction

terms.desc: Reinforcement Learning

Training a model on what people actually preferred rather than on text alone: collect demonstrations and fine-tune on them, then collect rankings of the model's own outputs and fine-tune again with reinforcement learning against those rankings. In the InstructGPT work a 1.3B model tuned this way was preferred to 175B GPT-3 — a hundred times larger.
terms.source: Ouyang et al., "Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback", arXiv:2203.02155 (March 2022)

terms.desc: Squared root of MSE
Normalization variant that's more stable than LayerNorm; used in modern LLMs like Llama.
Recurrent Neural Network
Commonly used transformer-based language model.
Curve that plots TPR versus FPR at different parameter settings
AMD's open-source GPU computing platform; CUDA alternative for non-NVIDIA accelerators.
Return on Investment
Positional encoding using rotation matrices; better extrapolation than absolute position embeddings.
Call functions on another machine as if local.
Daily cap for API requests (tier-dependent).
API rate-limit metric for request throughput.
AWS object storage service for datasets, model checkpoints, and logs; extremely cost-effective at scale.
Software as a Service
An HTTP method whose defined meaning is essentially read-only — it does not alter server state. GET and HEAD are the everyday examples, which is why crawlers and prefetchers may call them freely.
terms.source: RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics" (IETF, June 2022), §9.2.1

terms.desc: Libraries/tools to integrate a service into your code.
Software Development Life Cycle
Software-Defined Radio
A versioning convention where MAJOR increments on incompatible API changes, MINOR on backward-compatible additions, and PATCH on backward-compatible bug fixes.
terms.source: Semantic Versioning 2.0.0
terms.misread: That a version number always carries those promises. Under major version zero (0.y.z) the spec says anything may change at any time and the public API should not be considered stable — so 0.x carries no compatibility guarantee at all.

terms.desc: Desribes training approach to convert sequences from one domain (e.g. sentences in English) to sequences in another domain (e.g. the same sentences translated to French).
Cloud model where you run code without managing servers; provider handles scaling and provisioning.
Training a pre-trained model on curated (prompt, response) pairs to teach a desired behavior before RLHF/DPO alignment. The most common first step in building an instruction-following chat model.
SSH File Transfer Protocol
A two-step process requires joint learning of sign language recognition and translation.

terms.expansion: A one to one translation from the single sign to the single gloss.
A task of full translation from the sign language into the spoken one
terms.desc: grammar and syntax are included.
Service-Level Agreement
Compact LLM optimized for speed/cost/on-device use.
Service-Level Objective
an encoder transformer model trained to predict sign gloss sequences it takes spatial embeddings and learns spatio-temporal representations.
A full translation of signs to a spoken language.
an autoregressive transformer decoder model trained on output from SLRT to predict one word at a time to generate the corresponding spoken language sentence.
Secrets Manager
Integrated circuit combining CPU, GPU, memory, and other components on a single chip; used in mobile devices.

A self-organizing map (SOM) or self-organizing feature map (SOFM) is an unsupervised machine learning technique used to produce a low-dimensional (typically two-dimensional) representation of a higher dimensional data set while preserving the topological structure of the data
State of the Art
Inference technique where smaller model generates candidates verified by larger model; speeds up generation.
Temporary cloud VM purchased at discounted rates; can be reclaimed with short notice by cloud provider.
Global explainability method using spectral clustering and local explanations (LRP).
Language for relational databases.
A type of object detector that consists of a single stage. Some examples are YOLO RetinaNet and EfficientDet.

A browser feature letting a server push messages to a page over an ordinary HTTP response, using the EventSource interface and the text/event-stream format. One direction only, server to page — that is the trade against WebSocket, and it is why SSE is simpler.
terms.source: WHATWG HTML Standard, "Server-sent events"
terms.misread: That SSE is its own protocol. It is an API and a wire format defined in the HTML Standard, carried over plain HTTP.

terms.desc: Secure Shell
Secure Sockets Layer
Sequence modeling approach as alternative to transformers (e.g., Mamba); linear complexity in sequence length.
Single Sign-On

An attack where the attacker makes the *server* fetch a URL of their choosing, reaching internal resources the attacker could never reach directly — cloud metadata endpoints, internal databases, local files.
terms.source: OWASP, "Server Side Request Forgery"
terms.misread: That the leading S makes it a variant of CSRF. The forged request comes from the server, not the victim's browser, and the payoff is internal network access rather than an unwanted user action.

terms.desc: An algorithm that allows to tranfer properties of one object to another (i.e. transfer painitning style to a photography).
A method using style transfer to augment dataset.
Sending response in chunks rather than waiting for completion; enables real-time LLM output display.
When enabled, model must match your JSON schema exactly for tool args.
Speech-To-Text
Scalable Vector Graphics
Supervised learning models with associated learning algorithms that analyze data for classification and regression analysis.
Supervised learning models with associated learning algorithms that analyze data for regression analysis.
Attention restricted to local window; reduces complexity from quadratic to linear in sequence length.
Benchmark of real GitHub issues requiring code changes; evaluates end-to-end software engineering ability.
NVIDIA form factor for data center GPUs; uses integrated power and cooling for dense deployments.
Highest-priority instruction that sets assistant behavior.

A special instruction block sent to an LLM before the user's message to configure its persona, rules, and capabilities. Separate from the user turn in the chat format. Cached separately in providers that support prompt caching.
Transformer based language model that uses a text-to-text approach.

The transport protocol that turns an unreliable network into a reliable, in-order stream of bytes. It detects lost packets using sequence numbers and corrupted ones using checksums, then retransmits. Connections are set up by a three-way handshake before any data moves.
terms.source: RFC 9293, "Transmission Control Protocol (TCP)" (IETF, August 2022) — obsoletes RFC 793

terms.desc: Maximum heat output (in watts) a processor generates; determines cooling and power requirements.

Sampling hyperparameter controlling randomness of model outputs. At 0 the model is greedy (always picks the most probable token); at 1.0 it samples proportional to raw probabilities; above 1.0 outputs become increasingly random. Typical creative range: 0.7–1.0; code generation: 0.0–0.2.
Splitting model tensors across GPUs; each GPU computes partial results requiring communication.
NVIDIA's inference optimizer and runtime; compiles and optimizes models for NVIDIA GPUs.
Infrastructure-as-Code tool for declaratively managing cloud resources; supports AWS, GCP, Azure.

Test-time compute is the computational effort a model uses to refine an answer after receiving a prompt. Increasing this effort can let a model explore alternatives, verify intermediate steps, or correct mistakes before responding. It can improve performance on complex tasks without changing the model’s trained parameters.
One trillion floating-point operations; used to measure GPU and accelerator throughput (TFLOP/s).
Hugging Face's production-ready LLM serving framework with optimizations for latency and throughput.
Too Long; Didn't Read

The protocol that protects traffic between two applications over the internet — the S in HTTPS. It provides three things: the server is authenticated (so you know who you are talking to), the data is confidential, and tampering is detectable.
terms.source: RFC 8446, "The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3" (IETF, August 2018)
terms.misread: That TLS only encrypts. Authentication and integrity matter just as much — encryption alone would still let an impostor answer you.

terms.desc: Proportion of actual negatives that are correctly predicted
Model's internal text unit (not exactly words).

Process of splitting text into tokens (subword units) before passing to an LLM. Modern models use Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) or SentencePiece. Tokens are roughly 3/4 of a word on average; 1K tokens ≈ 750 words. GPT-4 uses ~100K token vocabulary (cl100k_base).

Mechanism allowing an LLM to request the execution of external functions (search, code runner, API calls) and receive the results back into context. The model outputs a structured function call; the host app executes it and passes results back. Core primitive for agents. OpenAI calls it 'function calling'; Anthropic calls it 'tool use'.
Model can request a tool execution (web search, file search, custom tools).

Sampling strategy selecting from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p. At p=0.9 the model only considers tokens that together account for 90% of the probability mass, dynamically adjusting the candidate pool size. Often used alongside Temperature.

Prompting strategy where the model generates multiple reasoning branches simultaneously, evaluates them, and selects the best path. Extends Chain-of-Thought to a search tree rather than a single linear chain. Strong on math and planning.
Daily cap for tokens (tier-dependent).
API rate-limit metric for tokens throughput.
Proportion of actual positives that are correctly predicted

Output throughput of an LLM inference system — how many tokens are generated per second after the first token arrives. Measures sustained speed. Groq's LPU achieves 800+ TPS; typical GPU APIs run 30-120 TPS.
Google's custom-designed AI accelerator for TensorFlow workloads; optimized for matrix operations at scale.
Logging every step/tool call for debugging and audit.

The neural network architecture nearly every modern language model is built on. Its point was subtractive: it dispensed with recurrence and convolutions entirely and relied on attention alone, which is what made training parallelisable at scale.
terms.source: Vaswani et al., "Attention Is All You Need", arXiv:1706.03762 (June 2017)

terms.desc: NVIDIA's inference server supporting multiple frameworks; simplifies model deployment with batching and metrics.
NVIDIA's specialized LLM inference framework building on TensorRT; enables fast inference on various hardware.

Latency between sending a request and receiving the very first output token from the model. Critical for perceived responsiveness in streaming UIs — a low TTFT makes the app feel instant even if total generation is slow.
Technology that converts written text to natural-sounding audio. Neural TTS models (ElevenLabs, Cartesia, OpenAI TTS) produce human-quality voice. Key metrics: MOS (Mean Opinion Score), latency.
User Interface

A method of knowledge transfer that enables models to acquire generalizable features without human guidance. This process involves training a smaller model on the output of a pre-trained, more complex model. By aligning their weights and behaviors through minimization, the smaller models learn a distilled version of the larger model's capabilities, allowing them to generalize across a wide range of tasks.

A compact string that identifies a resource, abstract or physical. URI is the general category; URL is the subset that also tells you how to reach the thing. The spec's own advice is to say "URI" rather than "URL" or "URN" in new writing.
terms.source: RFC 3986, "Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax" (IETF, January 2005)

terms.desc: The subset of URIs that, as well as identifying a resource, describes how to get to it — its access mechanism or network location. Every URL is a URI; not every URI is a URL.
terms.source: RFC 3986, "Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax" (IETF, January 2005), §1.1.3
terms.misread: That URL and URI are interchangeable. They are nested, not equal: URL is the narrower term.

terms.desc: A URI under the "urn" scheme, meant to stay globally unique and persistent as a name even after the thing it names is gone or unreachable. It identifies without locating.
terms.source: RFC 3986, "Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax" (IETF, January 2005), §1.1.3

terms.desc: Your instruction/request to the model.
The reference time scale that all internet timestamps state their offset from. A trailing Z on a timestamp means the offset is zero — the time is already in UTC.
terms.source: RFC 3339, "Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps" (IETF, July 2002), §1–2

terms.desc: The dominant text encoding: one to four bytes per character, covering the whole Unicode range. Its decisive property is that plain ASCII text is already valid UTF-8 unchanged, so older tools kept working — which is most of why it won.
terms.source: RFC 3629, "UTF-8, a transformation format of ISO 10646" (IETF, November 2003)
terms.misread: That the 8 means eight bits per character. It is the code unit size; characters take one to four of them.

terms.desc: Universally Unique Identifier
User Experience
3D image segmentation based on a volumetric fully convolutional neural network
An artificial neural network architecture belonging to the families of probabilistic graphical models and variational Bayesian methods.
Stores vectors and supports similarity search for retrieval.

Database optimized for storing and querying high-dimensional embedding vectors using approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search. Core infrastructure for RAG. Examples: Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate, Chroma, pgvector (Postgres extension). Enables semantic similarity search at scale.
Popular deep convolutional model designed for classification.

An LLM serving system built on PagedAttention, aimed at wasting as little key-value cache memory as possible and sharing it flexibly between requests. The paper reports 2–4× the throughput of comparable systems at the same latency.
terms.source: Kwon et al., "Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention", arXiv:2309.06180 (September 2023)

terms.desc: Multimodal model that processes both images and text. Accepts image+text input and produces text output. Examples: GPT-4o Vision, Claude 3 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, LLaVA, Phi-3 Vision.
Virtual Machine
Isolated cloud network with configurable subnets, firewalls, and routing; provides network segmentation.
Virtual Private Network
Specialized hardware for computer vision tasks like object detection and image classification.
Virtual Reality
GPU memory separate from CPU RAM; critical bottleneck for model size and batch processing.
Popular extensible code editor.
Large circular slice of silicon from which individual dies are cut; standard unit in semiconductor manufacturing.

A journalling mode that inverts the usual arrangement: instead of copying the old data aside and writing changes into the database, the original stays put and changes are appended to a separate WAL file, with a commit recorded by appending a marker. Readers and a writer can then proceed at the same time. In SQLite it has been available since version 3.7.0 (2010).
terms.source: SQLite documentation, "Write-Ahead Logging"
terms.misread: That WAL is strictly faster. SQLite lists real costs: it will not work over a network filesystem because it needs shared memory between processes, read-heavy workloads can be marginally slower, and very large transactions are usually better off in rollback mode.

terms.desc: Gradually increasing learning rate at training start to stabilize optimization and avoid divergence.

Embedding a statistical signal in model outputs (text, image, audio) that is imperceptible to humans but detectable by algorithms. Used to attribute AI-generated content and detect deepfakes. Techniques: logit-based (text), DCT embedding (images).
Waveform Audio File Format
The W3C's recommendation for making web content accessible, organised into testable success criteria at three conformance levels. WCAG 2.2 became a W3C Recommendation on 12 December 2024.
terms.source: W3C, "Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2", W3C Recommendation 12 December 2024
terms.misread: That reaching the top level makes a site accessible to everyone. The guidelines say plainly that even AAA content will not be accessible to people with all types, degrees or combinations of disability, particularly cognitive, language and learning disabilities.

terms.desc: A JSON file holding a web application's metadata — name, icons, start URL, display mode, orientation, scope — so a browser can install and launch it like a native app.
terms.source: W3C, "Web Application Manifest", W3C Working Draft 13 August 2026

terms.desc: HTTP callback allowing event-driven notifications; service POSTs data to client URL on events.

A protocol giving a browser and a server one persistent, two-way connection, so either side can send at any time. It exists because the alternative — repeatedly opening HTTP connections to poll for news — was wasteful and awkward.
terms.source: RFC 6455, "The WebSocket Protocol" (IETF, December 2011)

terms.desc: metric to measure performance used in NLP solutions e.g. in automatic speech recognition (ASR).
Work In Progress
A set of processes and methods to make machine learning algorithms and its results more interpretable.
Extensible Markup Language
Intel's unified GPU architecture combining performance and efficiency cores for diverse workloads.

An attack where a site is tricked into sending an attacker's script to another user's browser. Because the browser believes the script came from a site it trusts, the script runs with that trust and can reach cookies and session tokens.
terms.source: OWASP, "Cross Site Scripting (XSS)"
terms.misread: That a read-only or purely informational site cannot be seriously hurt by XSS. OWASP calls this out directly — reflected XSS can be severe on sites with no accounts and no transactions.

terms.desc: YAML Ain't Markup Language
Fast object detection algorithm.
Technique partitioning optimizer states, gradients, and model parameters across GPUs; core to DeepSpeed.

Prompting a model to perform a task it has never seen explicit examples of — relying entirely on instruction-following capability from pre-training and alignment. GPT-4 and Claude perform many tasks well zero-shot that older models needed fine-tuning for.
No examples provided; model solves from instruction alone.
